title: Rail Vikas Nigam Ltd - 542649 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: RVNL Q2 FY27 consolidated PAT rose 59% QoQ to INR 253.7 crore, while H1 revenue was flat at INR 9,022 crore and order book stood at INR 90,099 crore.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 revenue from operations was INR 4,700 crore, up 8.79% QoQ, and consolidated PAT rose 59.04% QoQ to INR 253.7 crore (up 10.06% YoY). Consolidated EBITDA was INR 294 crore at a 6.26% margin versus 4.4% in Q1. H1 revenue was essentially flat YoY (management cited 1.2% growth in one answer and a 0.11% decline in another), while H1 consolidated PAT grew 13.25% to INR 413 crore. Order book at 30 September 2026 was INR 90,099 crore, down from about INR 93,000 crore in Q1, as H1 inflow of INR 7,132 crore did not fully replace execution.

segments.name: Railways (order book)
segments.commentary: Railways account for INR 56,816 crore of the INR 90,099 crore order book, the largest segment.

segments.name: Signalling and telecom (order book)
segments.commentary: INR 12,224 crore of order book, including the BharatNet project (INR 13,236 crore, DBOM model, 82,607 km OSP).

segments.name: Building works
segments.commentary: INR 6,504 crore order book; contributed 33.53% of H1 FY27 revenue from operations, up 11% vs prior year. NMDC contract of INR 6,504 crore with INR 3,869 crore received in H1.

segments.name: Metros, power and transmission, ports/roads/highways, hydro/irrigation, other
segments.commentary: Order book of INR 5,346 crore (metros), INR 3,876 crore (power and transmission), INR 3,534 crore (ports, roads, highways), INR 1,237 crore (hydro and irrigation) and INR 562 crore (other works).

segments.name: Subsidiaries and JVs
segments.commentary: Subsidiaries contributed INR 56.11 crore to consolidated revenue and INR 6.36 crore to PAT in H1; share of JV/associate profit was INR 36.59 crore; dividend income from JVs and subsidiaries was INR 21.34 crore.

guidance_outlook: FY27 work order target of about INR 25,000 crore, in addition to existing order book; INR 7,132 crore received in H1. A later answer cited INR 20,000-25,000 crore.
FY27 top-line growth guidance of around 10% (stated as 10-15% in some answers); bottom-line growth of about 8-10%, with management saying 9-10%.
Core EBITDA margin target of 6-7% (excluding other income) for the year; management said next quarter would be better.
Management expects H2 to deliver about 60% of annual revenue, consistent with last year's pattern (H1 about 40%). Implied FY27 revenue of about INR 22,500-23,000 crore.

Near-term order pipeline: about INR 4,000 crore of railway works expected this month and INR 2,500 crore from NMDC in about two months; management cited roughly INR 10,000 crore in awards over one to two months.
Serbia (about INR 12,000 crore) and Israel Metro (about INR 10,000 crore RVNL share, eight packages of about INR 20,000 crore each) orders not expected this year; possibly next year.
capex_capacity: Vande Bharat sleeper train (INR 14,400 crore, 35-year maintenance) executed via SPV Kinet Railway with Russian partners; manufacturing at Latur factory; first prototype targeted for Q1 CY2027 (March-June 2027), after earlier slippage.
Rishikesh-Karnaprayag rail project (INR 37,119 crore, 125 km): 79% overall progress, about 97% tunnel excavation complete, targeted completion December 2029.
NMDC contract (INR 6,504 crore) work started; LOAs of about INR 3,000 crore issued.
Equity participation in multimodal logistics parks in Chennai and Bangalore.
Revenue per employee rose to INR 10.22 crore in Q2 from INR 9.6 crore in Q1.
demand_pricing: Order inflow in H1 FY27 was INR 7,132 crore (some answers cite about INR 7,500-7,600 crore); about 41% from NMDC PMC nomination and about 59% competitive bids.
Win rate on bids cited as 7-10% of contracts bid.
Management said bidding is aggressive, with focus on railways, highways, metros and international markets.

International: ongoing works in Maldives, Saudi Arabia, Rwanda; prequalified in Serbia and Israel Metro; L1 for Sierra Leone grant project of about INR 220 crore; pursuing Ghana and other African markets.
Closed South African subsidiary and Kyrgyz JV (both described as non-starters); JVs in Saudi Arabia and Uzbekistan retained; planning new JVs in Serbia and Romania.
Defence opportunity in pipeline; management hopes an EOI will be issued this financial year, with bidding to follow. No details disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: Status of international ports and harbours projects, and why RVNL is not moving ahead with them?
qa_highlights.answer: Ongoing works in Maldives, Saudi Arabia and Rwanda; qualified in Serbia and Israel Metro; L1 in Sierra Leone (about INR 220 crore grant project); focus on Ghana and other African countries.

qa_highlights.question: Vande Bharat readiness after repeated delays; is December 2026 the final deadline?
qa_highlights.answer: Teething issues over departmental approvals now resolved; manufacturing in progress at Latur; first prototype expected Q1 or at latest Q2 CY2027; only first prototype delayed, with contract timelines maintained thereafter.

qa_highlights.question: Order win percentage given that most orders come via nomination?
qa_highlights.answer: Of about INR 7,500 crore inflow, about 41% was NMDC PMC nomination (about INR 3,800 crore) and 59% competitive; bid win rate 7-10%.

qa_highlights.question: Will FY27 achieve 10% growth in revenue and profit given H1 is flat?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said H1 is up about 9% on a combined basis and it expects 9-10% growth for the year, with Q3 and Q4 carrying most execution; H1 revenue was flat (about 1.2% growth in one answer).

qa_highlights.question: Why is H1 revenue flat and the margin of about 5.6% in Q2 sustainable; any one-offs?
qa_highlights.answer: Revenue flat due to project closure in KSA (-0.11%); management targets 6-7% core margin (excluding other income) and expects improvement in Q3.

qa_highlights.question: Serbia and Israel order sizes and timing?
qa_highlights.answer: Orders not expected this year; Israel Metro eight packages of about INR 20,000 crore each, RVNL share about INR 10,000 crore; Serbia about INR 12,000 crore; both with JV partners.

qa_highlights.question: Is RVNL stepping back from international markets after closing South Africa and Kyrgyz subsidiaries?
qa_highlights.answer: Only two subsidiaries closed (Kyrgyzstan non-starter, South Africa not progressing); other JVs retained; new JVs planned in Serbia and Romania; logistics parks in Chennai and Bangalore.

risks_watch: H1 revenue flat YoY (management cited about 1.2% growth in one answer and a 0.11% decline in another); FY27 growth of 10-15% top line and 8-10% bottom line depends on H2 delivering about 60% of annual revenue.

Order book fell from about INR 93,000 crore in Q1 to INR 90,099 crore at 30 September 2026, with H1 inflow of INR 7,132 crore; the INR 25,000 crore FY27 order target needs about INR 10,000 crore of awards in the next one to two months per management.
Vande Bharat sleeper: first prototype now targeted for Q1 CY2027 (March-June 2027) or at latest Q2; management said the delay is for the prototype only, with contract timelines maintained.
Core EBITDA margin target of 6-7% excluding other income versus Q2 consolidated margin of 6.26% (Q1 4.4%); sustainability of Q2 margin unclear, as no one-offs were quantified.

International pipeline: Serbia (about INR 12,000 crore) and Israel Metro (about INR 10,000 crore RVNL share) not expected this year; Sierra Leone L1 of about INR 220 crore; new JVs planned in Serbia and Romania.
Defence opportunity still at pipeline stage with no details; management expects an EOI this financial year. Bid win rate cited at 7-10%.
key_quotes: So, if you see our H1 results, we are up by almost 9% QoQ. H1 to H1, if you compare, we are up by almost 9%.
It will definitely improve. We are targeting 6-7% margin, and we are hopeful to achieve that.
Definitely, there's a delay, but I think this delay is only for the first prototype.
And in Serbia and Israel, we have just been prequalified, so these orders will definitely not materialize this year.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the forward view (10-15% top-line growth, 9-10% bottom-line, H2-weighted execution) but was cautious and vague on specifics. Several answers gave inconsistent figures (H1 revenue change, FY27 order target, growth range), and it deferred details on defence, Serbia and Israel, and the Vande Bharat prototype timeline.

adds.what: Vande Bharat sleeper train manufacturing at Latur factory (INR 14,400 crore contract via SPV Kinet Railway); first prototype targeted

growth.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 10% (cut from ~15%) and PAT growth of 8-10%, backed by the INR 90,099 crore order book and a pipeline of about INR 10,000 crore in near-term awards, but the FY27 INR 25,000 crore order inflow target is only 28% achieved in H1 (INR 7,132 crore) and no own capacity additions were quantified.

oneOffs.what: Q2 consolidated margin of 6.26% (vs 4.4% in Q1) with no one-offs quantified; management targets 6-7% core margin excluding other income, so Q2 margin may be above the recurring level
Revenue drag from closure of KSA project (-0.11% on H1 revenue); a project closure is a non-recurring drag on H1 growth, not quantified

quality.why: Q2 PAT rose 10.06% YoY and H1 revenue was flat (about -0.11% to +1.2%), so the growth story is weak; the brief does not state the main driver of growth, and the sharp QoQ profit jump rests on a margin recovery (4.4% to 6.26%) whose sustainability management has not explained.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Core EBITDA margin rose to 6.26% in Q2 from 4.4% in Q1 and management targets 6-7% core margin (ex other income) for the year, saying Q3 will be better, though no one-offs were quantified.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: No own plant or line additions were quantified; the Vande Bharat Latur manufacturing is contract execution, with the first prototype slipping to Q1-Q2 CY2027.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Management guides FY27 revenue growth of about 10% with H2 delivering about 60% of annual revenue (implied INR 22,500-23,000 crore), but H1 revenue was flat at INR 9,022 crore and the order book fell to INR 90,099 crore from about INR 93,000 crore.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex or capacity expansion was not discussed in the brief beyond existing projects.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management cut FY27 top-line growth to about 10% from about 15%, and the H1 revenue trend is flat, so an upgrade looks unlikely.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: FY27 growth of 10% and PAT growth of 8-10% depend on H2 delivering about 60% of revenue, and the INR 25,000 crore order target needs about INR 10,000 crore of awards in one to two months against INR 7,132 crore received in H1.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Vande Bharat sleeper first prototype (INR 14,400 crore contract, Latur factory) is targeted for Q1-Q2 CY2027 after earlier slippage, though management says only the prototype is delayed.

rows.label: Near-term order awards of about INR 10,000 crore
rows.why: Management cited about INR 4,000 crore of railway works this month and INR 2,500 crore from NMDC in about two months, against an INR 25,000 crore FY27 target with INR 7,132 crore won in H1.

rows.label: International JVs and Sierra Leone grant project
rows.why: New JVs planned in Serbia and Romania and an L1 position on a Sierra Leone grant project of about INR 220 crore, while Serbia (about INR 12,000 crore) and Israel Metro (about INR 10,000 crore RVNL share) orders are not expected this year.

rows.label: Defence EOI and bidding
rows.why: Management hopes an EOI is issued this financial year with bidding to follow, but no details were disclosed and the bid win rate is 7-10%.

tone.note: Management was confident on the H2-weighted growth path and the 6-7% margin target but cautious and vague on specifics, with inconsistent H1 revenue and order-target figures and deferred answers on defence, Serbia/Israel and the Vande Bharat timeline; analysts pressed on flat H1 revenue, margin sust
